ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $OC$ is the bisector of $\angle AOD$, and $OE$ is the bisector of $\angle BOD$. If $\angle AOB=140^\circ$, then what is the degree measure of $\angle COE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $OC$ is the bisector of $\angle AOD$ and $OE$ is the bisector of $\angle BOD$,\\
$\therefore \angle COD=\frac{1}{2}\angle AOD$, $\angle DOE=\frac{1}{2}\angle BOD$,\\
Given that $\angle AOB=140^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle AOD+\angle BOD=140^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle COE=\angle COD+\angle DOE=\frac{1}{2}\left(\angle AOD+\angle BOD\right)=\frac{1}{2}\times 140^\circ=\boxed{70^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, all rays start from point O, OB is above, OD is roughly to the right, and OA is in the lower right; ray OD is located inside the large angle formed by OA and OB. Ray C is located between OA and OD, and ray E is located between OD and OB, so the angle from OC turning to OE passes through OD, and can be regarded as the sum of ∠COD and ∠DOE. Reasoning: Let ∠AOD = x, ∠BOD = y. It can be seen from the figure that OD is between OA and OB, so x + y = ∠AOB = 140°. Because OC is the angle bisector of ∠AOD, ∠COD = x/2; because OE is the angle bisector of ∠BOD, ∠DOE = y/2. Also because D is between C and E, ∠COE = ∠COD + ∠DOE = x/2 + y/2 = (x+y)/2 = 140°/2 = 70°.
